title: Security architecture, technology and controls
summary: Ask informed governance questions about identity, boundaries, controls and recoverable service design.
outcomes: Read a service architecture for trust and information flows.
Evaluate preventive, detective and recovery controls through evidence.

realExample.title: Protective DNS at public-sector scale
realExample.documentedOutcome: The UK's NCSC 2024 review reported that Protective DNS had handled more than 2.5 trillion requests and prevented access to 1.5 million malicious domains since 2017.
realExample.discussion: Use the delivered service to examine the role and limits of a shared protective control, including coverage, legitimate-site handling and complementary controls.
realExample.scope: A UK public-sector control example. It does not create a South African legal requirement or prove protection against every attack.

units.title: Read the architecture as a set of trust decisions
objectives: Identify trust boundaries and sensitive flows.

chapters.title: Draw what information crosses which boundary
chapters.bodyHtml:
A governance architecture view need not be a network-engineering diagram. Show the citizen channel, staff application, identity service, data stores, external providers, administration and recovery. Label the information crossing each boundary and the authority for the transfer.

Ask what each component trusts. Does the application trust a supplied record identifier without checking the user's permission? Can supplier support reach every data store? Does a recovery process depend on the same unavailable identity service? These questions expose design assumptions.

Keep the diagram tied to an actual service version. A supplier's generic reference architecture may omit the department's configuration and integrations. Record the important differences and the owner who can explain them.

chapters.title: Identity, permission and accountability are distinct
chapters.bodyHtml:
Authentication establishes an identity or credential claim; authorisation determines what that identity may do. A successful sign-in does not imply permission to view every citizen's record. Least privilege limits access to the authorised task, and separation of duties can protect consequential changes.

Multifactor authentication adds protection to sign-in when independent factors are properly used, but it does not repair excessive permissions or a broken approval process. Two knowledge secrets are not automatically two different factor categories. Protect recovery and reset routes as part of the identity system.

NIST's zero-trust architecture guidance is useful optional technical background: network location alone should not create implicit trust. It is not a product certificate or a replacement for South African authority. The DISO should ask how the actual resource request is authorised and how a revoked need takes effect.

chapters.title: Cloud and suppliers need an explicit boundary
chapters.bodyHtml:
A service contract should explain which party manages identities, configuration, logging, backup, recovery, patching and exit. A provider may secure its platform while the department remains responsible for account permissions and information use.

Identify remote support routes and approved functionality. A secure connection can still expose too much if the connected account has unnecessary privilege. Assess who approves it, what is logged, who reviews activity and how access ends.

Ask for a usable exit and recovery path: complete information, configuration, documentation and the ability to operate or transfer the service. A design that only the supplier can understand creates a material continuity and bargaining dependency.

application.title: Review the fictional provincial licensing architecture
application.instructionsHtml:
A citizen portal sends applications to a cloud case system. Staff sign in with MFA, but every clerk can edit all payment details. Supplier support uses a permanent administrator connection. Backup recovery requires the same identity platform that the continuity plan assumes is down.

Spend about 60 minutes drawing the boundaries and identifying five design decisions for the responsible owners.
application.deliverable: An annotated architecture and five decision records.
application.suggestedAnswerHtml:
Identify permission scope separately from MFA. Restrict payment changes and define independent approval where the service requires it.

Bound supplier access and retain its approval/review/exit path. Analyse the recovery dependency on identity rather than treating backup existence as sufficient.

Name owners and evidence for each decision. Propose service-preserving controls rather than a blanket shutdown.

reflection.prompt: Which architecture assumption would fail if your identity provider were unavailable?
reflection.guidanceHtml: Identify one authorised recovery path and the owner who can verify it.

quiz.title: Read the architecture as a set of trust decisions — knowledge check

questions.name: M08-U01-Q01
questions.promptHtml: A user signs in successfully. What must still be checked for a record request?

answers.textHtml: Whether that user is authorised for that record and action
answers.feedbackHtml: Authentication and authorisation answer different questions.

answers.textHtml: Nothing because authentication grants all access
answers.feedbackHtml: Identity is not universal permission.

answers.textHtml: Only whether the network is internal
answers.feedbackHtml: Location alone does not establish the business authority.

answers.textHtml: Only whether the password was recently changed
answers.feedbackHtml: Password age does not define record access.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Authentication and authorisation answer different questions.

questions.name: M08-U01-Q02
questions.promptHtml: MFA is enabled but every clerk can edit payment details. What remains?

answers.textHtml: Excessive authorisation and possible separation-of-duty weakness
answers.feedbackHtml: A sign-in control does not replace permission design.

answers.textHtml: No material issue because MFA is present
answers.feedbackHtml: MFA does not define permitted actions.

answers.textHtml: Only an availability issue
answers.feedbackHtml: The described concern is unauthorised change.

answers.textHtml: A need to remove all authentication
answers.feedbackHtml: That would worsen protection.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: A sign-in control does not replace permission design.

questions.name: M08-U01-Q03
questions.promptHtml: What makes an architecture diagram useful for governance?

answers.textHtml: Actual information flows, boundaries, dependencies and owners
answers.feedbackHtml: Review the actual service architecture.

answers.textHtml: Only a generic supplier product diagram
answers.feedbackHtml: It may omit the local configuration.

answers.textHtml: Only the number of network devices
answers.feedbackHtml: That does not explain trust decisions.

answers.textHtml: A future target diagram labelled as current
answers.feedbackHtml: That confuses proposed and operating design.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Review the actual service architecture.

questions.name: M08-U01-Q04
questions.promptHtml: A backup restore requires the identity service that is unavailable. What is this?

answers.textHtml: A recovery dependency that needs an authorised alternative
answers.feedbackHtml: Recovery must include dependencies and access.

answers.textHtml: Proof that the backup file is corrupt
answers.feedbackHtml: The problem may be access rather than file integrity.

answers.textHtml: An issue solved solely by adding more backup copies
answers.feedbackHtml: Copies do not remove the identity dependency.

answers.textHtml: A reason to share administrator credentials permanently
answers.feedbackHtml: That is an uncontrolled workaround.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Recovery must include dependencies and access.

questions.name: M08-U01-Q05
questions.promptHtml: What does zero-trust guidance primarily challenge in this context?

answers.textHtml: Implicit trust based only on network location
answers.feedbackHtml: Use the guidance within its technical scope.

answers.textHtml: That an internal network can replace resource-specific authorisation
answers.feedbackHtml: Zero-trust guidance challenges implicit trust based on location alone.

answers.textHtml: That every successful authentication permits every service action
answers.feedbackHtml: Authentication does not establish all permissions.

answers.textHtml: That location-based trust must be replaced by unrestricted public access
answers.feedbackHtml: The guidance concerns deliberate trust and access decisions, not removal of controls.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Use the guidance within its technical scope.

questions.name: M08-U01-Q06
questions.promptHtml: Which supplier responsibility should be clarified before adoption?

answers.textHtml: Who configures access, retains logs and restores the departmental service
answers.feedbackHtml: Shared services need explicit responsibility boundaries.

answers.textHtml: Only whether the supplier owns a data centre
answers.feedbackHtml: That does not allocate all service controls.

answers.textHtml: Only the vendor's general certification name
answers.feedbackHtml: Its scope may not cover local responsibilities.

answers.textHtml: Only the first month's subscription cost
answers.feedbackHtml: That omits operational obligations.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Shared services need explicit responsibility boundaries.

questions.name: M08-U01-Q07
questions.promptHtml: Which observations identify a trust-boundary issue? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: A supplied record ID is used without checking the caller's permission
answers.feedbackHtml: The application trusts an unverified access claim.

answers.textHtml: Supplier support can reach unrelated datasets
answers.feedbackHtml: The boundary permits unnecessary scope.

answers.textHtml: A policy document has been approved
answers.feedbackHtml: That alone says nothing about the boundary.

answers.textHtml: Staff use a familiar interface
answers.feedbackHtml: Familiarity does not establish trust handling.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Inspect the actual request and permitted reach.

questions.name: M08-U01-Q08
questions.promptHtml: Which features strengthen a supplier exit plan? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: Complete information and configuration export
answers.feedbackHtml: These support a usable transition.

answers.textHtml: Named responsibilities for transfer and access revocation
answers.feedbackHtml: These make exit actionable.

answers.textHtml: A promise that the supplier will never change
answers.feedbackHtml: That is not a recoverable plan.

answers.textHtml: Only screenshots of the current service
answers.feedbackHtml: Screenshots do not preserve operation.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Exit planning reduces a concrete service dependency.

questions.name: M08-U01-Q09
questions.promptHtml: Two passwords are automatically two independent authentication-factor categories.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. Both are knowledge secrets; factor independence requires more than two prompts.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: Both are knowledge secrets; factor independence requires more than two prompts.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Both are knowledge secrets; factor independence requires more than two prompts.

questions.name: M08-U01-Q10
questions.promptHtml: A secure remote connection can still grant excessive privilege.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: Transport protection and authorisation are distinct.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. Transport protection and authorisation are distinct.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Transport protection and authorisation are distinct.

questions.name: M08-U01-Q11
questions.promptHtml: Match the design term to its question.

pairs.answer: Who or what is presenting this identity?
Can the consequential action be attributed and examined?
Where does a different authority or exposure begin?

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Each question reveals a different design concern.

questions.name: M08-U01-Q12
questions.promptHtml: Successful authentication does not replace resource-level [[1]] or appropriate [[2]].
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Identity proof must connect to permission and traceability.

units.title: Evaluate control coverage and operation
objectives: Distinguish preventive, detective and recovery controls.
Ask for representative evidence and maintenance.

chapters.title: Layer controls around the service consequence
chapters.bodyHtml:
Preventive controls reduce the chance of an unwanted action; detective controls help identify it; recovery controls restore a usable state. A service usually needs a combination. Restricted editing may prevent unauthorised changes, logs and reconciliation may detect them, and a recoverable history may support correction.

Choose layers that address the same consequence rather than buying overlapping products without a coverage question. If every control depends on the same administrator or identity provider, their apparent independence may be misleading.

The Protective DNS case shows a useful shared preventive layer. It can reduce access to known malicious destinations, but it does not establish the correctness of a payment approval or every device's configuration. Ask what population is covered, how exclusions are managed and what complementary controls are required.

chapters.title: Technical controls have operating dependencies
chapters.bodyHtml:
Encryption depends on correct configuration, key control and authorised use. If encrypted information can be opened by every shared account, disclosure risk remains. If recovery keys are unavailable during a disaster, encryption can also prevent legitimate recovery.

Patching requires knowledge of the actual assets, supported versions, exposure, testing and an authorised change route. A percentage based only on devices that reported successfully may hide unmanaged systems. Distinguish a planned update from one installed and functioning.

Logging requires relevant events, reliable time, protected records and a review or response process. Collecting every possible event without a purpose can increase cost and sensitive data exposure. Define the questions the logs must answer and preserve the applicable retention and access controls.

chapters.title: Use evidence to accept and maintain controls
chapters.bodyHtml:
Ask for evidence that matches the service and configuration: representative permission checks, actual patch status, recovery results, approved exceptions and observed alert handling. A product feature list describes capability, not necessarily the departmental implementation.

Include failure and change in the operating plan. Who notices that collection stopped, certificates expired, rules were disabled or a supplier interface changed? What happens if a control rejects legitimate service activity? The owner needs a safe correction route.

Maintain the control's relationship to the risk. When the service adds a new data flow or privileged function, reassess coverage. Keep the implementation, owner and evidence current enough that management can judge whether the control still supports its intended outcome.

application.title: Evaluate a proposed control package
application.instructionsHtml:
A fictional vendor offers endpoint software, encrypted backups and a dashboard. Its patch score excludes devices that have not checked in for 30 days. Backup keys are held only by one administrator. Alerts have no assigned response owner.

Spend about 60 minutes preparing an acceptance decision and a prioritised correction plan.
application.deliverable: A control-coverage table and acceptance conditions.
application.suggestedAnswerHtml:
Include non-reporting devices in the asset reconciliation and explain unknown status. Confirm recovery-key custody and demonstrate authorised recovery.

Assign alert triage, response and escalation, with useful event scope. Do not equate dashboard existence with detection capability.

Accept, defer or condition elements based on actual evidence and service needs. Preserve the vendor's capability claims separately from observed implementation.

reflection.prompt: Which security control would stop working quietly if one person left?
reflection.guidanceHtml: Identify the dependency and an accountable maintenance or recovery arrangement.

quiz.title: Evaluate control coverage and operation — knowledge check

questions.name: M08-U02-Q01
questions.promptHtml: Which is a detective control for unauthorised payment edits?

answers.textHtml: Reviewable change logs and payment reconciliation
answers.feedbackHtml: Detection identifies evidence of an unwanted action.

answers.textHtml: A rule preventing the edit before it occurs
answers.feedbackHtml: That is preventive.

answers.textHtml: A backup used after damage
answers.feedbackHtml: That is a recovery measure.

answers.textHtml: A purchase approval for a tool
answers.feedbackHtml: That is not an operating detection control.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Detection identifies evidence of an unwanted action.

questions.name: M08-U02-Q02
questions.promptHtml: A patch dashboard excludes devices silent for 30 days. What is the concern?

answers.textHtml: The denominator can hide unmanaged or unknown devices
answers.feedbackHtml: Define coverage and account for unknowns.

answers.textHtml: That the percentage measures verified compliance across the full estate without a coverage qualification
answers.feedbackHtml: The observed subset may exclude unmanaged or unknown devices.

answers.textHtml: That every silent device is compliant because it produced no alert
answers.feedbackHtml: No observation is not verified success.

answers.textHtml: That the measure can no longer be useful for the devices it actually covers
answers.feedbackHtml: The subset remains informative when its scope and limits are clear.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Define coverage and account for unknowns.

questions.name: M08-U02-Q03
questions.promptHtml: Encrypted backups have keys known only to one absent administrator. What remains at risk?

answers.textHtml: Authorised recoverability
answers.feedbackHtml: Key custody is part of recovery design.

answers.textHtml: Only confidentiality, because availability is unrelated to key custody
answers.feedbackHtml: Loss of authorised key access can prevent recovery.

answers.textHtml: No recovery issue, provided the encryption algorithm remains strong
answers.feedbackHtml: Algorithm strength does not make the key available to the recovery team.

answers.textHtml: Only the backup schedule, because knowing the key holder is sufficient
answers.feedbackHtml: A named but unavailable holder does not establish a usable recovery route.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Key custody is part of recovery design.

questions.name: M08-U02-Q04
questions.promptHtml: Which question best assesses a logging service?

answers.textHtml: Which required events are retained, reviewed and acted upon?
answers.feedbackHtml: Logging needs a purpose and response process.

answers.textHtml: How many raw events can be collected regardless of purpose?
answers.feedbackHtml: Volume alone is not useful detection.

answers.textHtml: Whether every employee can browse all logs
answers.feedbackHtml: That can create unnecessary exposure.

answers.textHtml: Whether logs can replace all preventive controls
answers.feedbackHtml: Detection does not prevent every action.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Logging needs a purpose and response process.

questions.name: M08-U02-Q05
questions.promptHtml: A product supports an access-control feature. What establishes departmental implementation?

answers.textHtml: Evidence of the actual configured permissions and operating process
answers.feedbackHtml: Assess the actual service, not only product capability.

answers.textHtml: The product's feature list alone
answers.feedbackHtml: Capability is not deployment.

answers.textHtml: The supplier's entire customer count
answers.feedbackHtml: That does not establish local configuration.

answers.textHtml: The renewal invoice
answers.feedbackHtml: Payment is not proof of control operation.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Assess the actual service, not only product capability.

questions.name: M08-U02-Q06
questions.promptHtml: What should happen when a control blocks legitimate critical service activity?

answers.textHtml: Use the authorised correction or exception route with assessed risk
answers.feedbackHtml: Protect the service through a controlled decision.

answers.textHtml: Disable it permanently without a record
answers.feedbackHtml: That loses protection and accountability.

answers.textHtml: Ignore the service consequence indefinitely
answers.feedbackHtml: Availability is part of the objective.

answers.textHtml: Assume all blocked activity is malicious
answers.feedbackHtml: Controls can produce false positives.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Protect the service through a controlled decision.

questions.name: M08-U02-Q07
questions.promptHtml: Which are necessary questions about encryption? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: Who can use and recover the keys?
answers.feedbackHtml: Keys determine effective access and recovery.

answers.textHtml: Which information and channels are actually covered?
answers.feedbackHtml: Coverage can differ from the product claim.

answers.textHtml: Whether a strong algorithm removes the need to control who can decrypt
answers.feedbackHtml: Key access and authorisation remain essential.

answers.textHtml: Whether a generic encryption statement proves that every copy and channel is covered
answers.feedbackHtml: Actual coverage must be established for the information flow.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Encryption is a configured control with dependencies.

questions.name: M08-U02-Q08
questions.promptHtml: Which evidence helps maintain a control? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: Alerting when collection or protection stops
answers.feedbackHtml: This detects loss of coverage.

answers.textHtml: Review after a new privileged service function is added
answers.feedbackHtml: The risk and required coverage may change.

answers.textHtml: Keeping the original report unchanged forever
answers.feedbackHtml: It can become stale.

answers.textHtml: Assuming maintenance belongs to an unnamed supplier
answers.feedbackHtml: Responsibilities must be explicit.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Controls need ongoing ownership and change review.

questions.name: M08-U02-Q09
questions.promptHtml: Preventive, detective and recovery layers can share a dependency that weakens their apparent independence.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: A common administrator or identity failure may affect several layers.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. A common administrator or identity failure may affect several layers.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: A common administrator or identity failure may affect several layers.

questions.name: M08-U02-Q10
questions.promptHtml: Protective DNS proves the correctness of a departmental payment approval.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. The control addresses a different part of the service.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: The control addresses a different part of the service.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: The control addresses a different part of the service.

questions.name: M08-U02-Q11
questions.promptHtml: Match the measure to its control role.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: A complete control design covers different stages of harm.

questions.name: M08-U02-Q12
questions.promptHtml: Place the control at its relevant service boundary. A is staff sign-in; B is the API's requested record and payment action; C is supplier support reaching selected datasets; D is the recovery site's need for usable keys and access.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Identity proof, resource-specific permission, scoped supplier access and usable recovery are distinct controls. A successful sign-in does not establish permission over every record or guarantee recovery.

background.alt: Place the control at its relevant service boundary. A is staff sign-in; B is the API's requested record and payment action; C is supplier support reaching selected datasets; D is the recovery site's need for usable keys and access.

drops.label: A: Staff sign in through the departmental identity service.
B: The API receives a record ID and a requested payment action.
C: Supplier support connects to selected departmental datasets.
D: The recovery site needs keys and access during an outage.
